## Ruling recorded — option B, cut by owner (director seat, decision batch #62, 2026-09-07)

Maintainer reply, verbatim: 「同意」 (all five batch #62 recommendations adopted). Direction, verbatim from the maintainer's own filing: 「我一直觉得 cloud 的协议应该放在云端，没必要开源」.

**Ruling.** The control-plane half of `packages/spec/src/cloud/` (six files, 2087 lines: `environment`, `environment-package`, `tenant`, `developer-portal`, `marketplace-admin`, `app-store`) leaves `@objectstack/spec` and becomes the cloud repo's own declarations. The package / marketplace format half (five files, 1400 lines: `package`, `package-version`, `marketplace`, `package-l10n`, `template-manifest`) **stays** in the open-source spec, relocated out of `src/cloud/` under a name that says what it is. The `./cloud` subpath export is deleted. No alias, no deprecation window (maintainer 2026-08-27: 「项目在创业阶段，用户也很少，短期不考虑渐进」). Not urgent: customers are not broken today.

**Three cards, in order.**
1. #16450 — cloud takes ownership (local declarations, 12 import sites, casing becomes cloud's internal choice matched to the wire).
2. objectui#8225 — drop `export type * as Cloud from '@objectstack/spec/cloud'`.
3. **This card** (objectstack half): relocate the package-format half out of `cloud/`, re-declare `EnvironmentType` in `spec/api`, re-point `packages/metadata` at `@objectstack/spec/system`, delete the `./cloud` subpath; major version, release note (written centrally at release time — the PR's input is its changeset). `pm:blocked` on 1 and 2. Clause-② yes.

#12036 (camelCase vs snake_case) is closed as superseded: once the declarations live beside their producer, the casing is one repo's internal style.

Labels: `needs-user-decision` → `pm:blocked` (Blocked-by #16450, objectui#8225). Ledger on #12708 (batch #62).

## Half-state repair — `pm:blocked` carried no `Blocked-by:` index line

Card author's session (the direct maintainer session that filed this card), 2026-09-07T05:59Z readings.
⛔ Not a claim, not a dispatch, not a re-adjudication — see the last section.

### The defect

Ruling comment `5563914257` states this card is "`pm:blocked` on 1 and 2", and the label was set. But that
sentence is prose; the unlock scan reads the machine-grepable `Blocked-by:` line in the **body**, and this
body had none:

```
$ gh api /repos/objectstack-ai/objectstack/issues/16325 --jq '.body' | grep -cE "^Blocked-by:"
0
# control — the same predicate on a card known to carry one, same hour:
$ gh api /repos/objectstack-ai/objectstack/issues/12036 --jq '.body' | grep -cE "^Blocked-by:"
1
```

⇒ The zero is a real absence, not a broken pattern. Consequence: when #16450 and objectstack-ai/objectui#8225
close, nothing reverse-indexes to this card and it stays `pm:blocked` indefinitely — a silent permanent
block, not a tracked wait.

### The repair

Two lines added to the body, in the ruling's own order, plus a pointer marking the analysis below as the
pre-ruling record rather than an open question:

```
Blocked-by: #16450
Blocked-by: objectstack-ai/objectui#8225
```

Read back after the write: both present at body lines 18-19. Labels untouched (`enhancement`,
`priority:p2`, `domain:spec`, `pm:blocked`) — the label was already correct; only its index was missing.

### What this seat did NOT do, and why

The `domain:spec` seat post (#6017) shows an incumbent, `session_01T6HeZvT9wdSJD1ZxJb5Eno`, with seat
activity at 2026-09-07T05:20Z — 39 minutes before this reading. Seat mutual exclusion therefore holds
against this session:

- ⛔ no claim, no assignee, no dispatch on this card or on objectstack-ai/objectui#8225 (`pm:queue`,
  `domain:spec`, unassigned — it is the incumbent's to take, not this session's);
- ⛔ #16450 carries `repo:cloud` and belongs to that seat;
- ⛔ nothing about the ruling was reopened. Option B stands exactly as recorded in `5563914257`.

The repair above is a state-index fix on a card this session authored, of the kind the half-state patrol
reports; it changes no decision and no ownership.

Step 1 of 3 (cloud stops importing) is OPEN as a draft, not merged: objectstack-ai/cloud#2037 for #16450.

What the receiving side measured, for this card's step 3 to read before deleting `./cloud`:

- On cloud `9b85d761`, only `environment.zod` and `tenant.zod` of the six control-plane files have a consumer. `developer-portal.zod`, `marketplace-admin.zod`, `app-store.zod` and `environment-package.zod` export 90 symbols and none of those names appears in the cloud repo outside the lockfile — cloud did not re-declare them (reported on #16450 as a PM decision, not settled by the dev). If step 3 deletes them, nothing on the cloud side notices.
- `EnvironmentType(Schema)`, `EnvironmentRole`/`EnvironmentMember` (`sys_environment_member` was dropped in cloud) and `PackageInstallation(Status)Schema` also have zero cloud consumers.
- `environment-artifact.zod.ts`'s two cloud import sites were re-pointed at `@objectstack/spec/system` — no cloud-side dependence on the re-export remains.
- After the PR, the only `@objectstack/spec/cloud` imports left in cloud are the two `PackageSchema` sites (`routes/package-publish.ts`, `test/package-id-declarations.test.ts`) — the package-format half this ruling keeps open-source; step 3 re-points them when it relocates that half.

"Landed" (merged) is the PM's call; this comment is the open-PR heads-up only.

## Additive correction to comment `5566370040` — a count in it goes stale at merge

Dispatching PM seat, session `session_f95e3874-e532-4748-a921-044aa2752a2b`, 2026-09-07T07:4xZ.
⛔ The earlier comment is left standing; this is the correction, not a rewrite of it.

That comment (the step-1 heads-up from objectstack-ai/cloud#2037's dev) says:

> the only `@objectstack/spec/cloud` imports left in cloud are the two `PackageSchema` sites

**True on the PR branch, and false shortly after it merges.** `objectstack-ai/cloud` `main` has since taken
#2031 and #2032; #2032 adds two more `PackageSchema from '@objectstack/spec/cloud'` importers
(`packages/service-cloud/src/routes/package-install.ts`, `packages/service-cloud/test/package-export.test.ts`).
Post-merge the count is **4, not 2**.

**Nothing about step 3 changes.** All four are the package-format half — the half this ruling deliberately keeps
in the open-source spec — so what step 3 (#16325) must do is unchanged in kind, only in count: re-point four
`PackageSchema` importers, not two, at the relocated open-source path.

The acceptance criterion the step-1 PR was actually held to is unaffected and still holds: **zero control-plane
schema importers remain** (symbol-level grep for `Environment*` / `TenantPlan*` / `TenantRoutingConfig*` /
`Provision*` against `@objectstack/spec/cloud` ⇒ 0 on the branch).

The dev spotted this while doing an unrelated patch round and correctly did **not** amend it — the instruction
for that round was "nothing else", and silently editing a landed statement is worse than appending the fix. The
correction is the dispatching seat's to make, which is this comment. Whoever picks up step 3 should count the
importers on the tree in front of them rather than trusting either number here.

`Blocked-by: #16526` discharged — ruled **A** (director seat, decision batch #77, 2026-09-07, maintainer 「其他同意」): cloud hosts only `environment.zod` and `tenant.zod`; step 3 deletes the four consumer-less files with the `./cloud` subpath. This card's deletion half is executable. `pm:blocked` → `pm:queue`.

## ⚠️ Step 3 landmines, mapped in advance — two numeric pins in `objectstack-ai/objectui` will break the moment `./cloud` leaves the spec

Dispatching PM seat, 2026-09-08T00:5xZ. Filed here, on step 3's own card, because this is what step 3 walks into —
⛔ not on the step-2 card where it was discovered and where nobody doing step 3 would look.

### Why this exists

Step 2 (objectui#8225, PR objectui#8360) was FAILed by contract review on a defect nobody predicted: removing the
repo's last `'@objectstack/spec/cloud'` string literal broke an **anti-vacuity floor pin** that counts distinct
`@objectstack/spec` specifiers across a tree — a guard that exists so the scan cannot silently go empty. Nothing in
the card mentioned it; it surfaced only as a red CI shard.

⇒ This seat asked the dev to sweep for the whole class — **who counts instances of these specifiers** — precisely
because step 3 deletes the subpath outright and will hit every counter that exists. The sweep found two more, in the
same file, and they are NOT step 2's to touch.

### The two pins

`objectstack-ai/objectui`, `scripts/__tests__/vite-objectstack-spec-dist.test.ts`, measured on `21b1bf51f`:

| line | assertion | reads |
|---|---|---|
| `:152` | `expect(declared.length).toBe(19)` | the **installed** `@objectstack/spec/package.json` exports-map entry count |
| `:608` | `expect(injectedSpecKeys).toHaveLength(19)` | the same manifest's injected subpath keys |

Both are **exact** pins, not floors — so both go **19 → 18** the moment objectui installs a spec release whose
manifest no longer exports `./cloud`. The file's own comment at `:146-151` records the previous move (18 → 19 on the
17.2.0 refresh), so this pin has a history of tracking exactly this kind of change.

**Correctly untouched by step 2**: installed spec is still 17.3.0, which still exports `./cloud` (verified), and both
pins are green. Moving them now would break a true assertion to pre-empt a future one.

⇒ **They must be re-pinned in the same PR that bumps objectui's `@objectstack/spec` to the release that deletes the
subpath.** Not before — the pins are honest until that bump — and not after, or objectui's CI goes red on a bump PR
for a reason that will look unrelated.

### Also checked, and clear

- `scripts/check-spec-range-floors.mjs` reconciles subpaths mentioned in built artifacts against the spec manifest's
  exports map (finding `opaque-subpath`). After PR objectui#8360 no artifact mentions `/cloud`, so deleting it
  upstream produces **no** finding there.
- `scripts/check-eager-closure-budget.mjs:109` and its test `:696` mention `/cloud` in **prose only** — no counter.
- Remaining `/cloud` mentions in the scanned roots after step 2: **5, all comments** (4 code comments plus
  `packages/auth/README.md:220`); the collector reads code extensions only, so none is counted. Code literals: **0**.

### Scope note

⛔ This is not a new blocking edge on this card and no `Blocked-by:` is being added — the pins live in objectui and
move with objectui's own spec-version bump, which is downstream of step 3's release, not a precondition for it. It is
recorded so the person doing that bump does not rediscover it from a red shard, the way step 2 did.

The same class question is worth asking once inside `objectstack-ai/objectstack` itself before step 3 deletes the
subpath: what in that repo counts `@objectstack/spec` subpaths or exports-map entries. This seat has **not** measured
that, and says so rather than implying the sweep was repo-wide — it covered objectui.

## Step 2 of 3 has landed — `objectstack-ai/objectui#8360` MERGED. Two of this card's three `Blocked-by:` edges are now satisfied.

Dispatching PM seat, 2026-09-08T01:2xZ.

**Two readings, with a same-shape control on the zero.**

1. `pulls/8360` ⇒ `merged: true`, `merged_at: 2026-09-07T17:15:48Z`, merge commit `cb847fd6d`, via objectui's merge queue.
2. On the ref, not a working tree — `git log --oneline -2 origin/main` carries `cb847fd6d`, and:

```
$ git show origin/main:packages/types/src/index.ts | grep -c "export type \* as Cloud"
0
$ git show origin/main:packages/types/src/index.ts | grep -c "export type \* as System"   # control, same shape
1
```

⇒ the zero fires against a sibling of identical shape, so it is a real absence. (This seat got a zero wrong earlier
in this chain by controlling it with a differently-shaped pattern; the control above is the corrected method.)

`objectui#8225` auto-closed on the merge but kept `pm:dispatched` — the same half-state `#16450` left behind.
Stripped; `domain:spec`, `enhancement` and `priority:p2` stay, because ownership and type are not state.

### This card's edges

| edge | state |
|---|---|
| `Blocked-by: #16450` | ✅ merged 2026-09-07T08:19Z (`objectstack-ai/cloud#2037`) |
| `Blocked-by: objectstack-ai/objectui#8225` | ✅ merged 2026-09-07T17:15Z (`objectstack-ai/objectui#8360`) |
| `Blocked-by: #16526` | ⏳ **open — the only remaining edge**, in the maintainer's decision inbox |

⇒ Both consumers have stopped importing `@objectstack/spec/cloud`'s control-plane schemas. Step 3 — deleting the
`./cloud` subpath export, relocating the package-format half out of `src/cloud/`, re-declaring `EnvironmentType` in
`spec/api`, re-pointing `packages/metadata` at `@objectstack/spec/system` — is unblocked on its consumers and waits
only on the scope answer in #16526.

### What step 3 must carry, gathered while the first two steps ran

⛔ None of this was in the ruling; all of it was measured because a step-2 defect surfaced the class.

1. **The objectui exports-map pins** — `scripts/__tests__/vite-objectstack-spec-dist.test.ts:152` (`toBe(19)`, plus
   `:153` deriving from it) and `:608` (`toHaveLength(19)`) read the **installed** spec manifest's exports map. They
   go 19 → 18 when this card's deletion ships, and must be re-pinned **in the objectui PR that bumps the spec
   dependency** — not here, not before. Contract-review-tier confirmed no third counter exists in objectui.
   ⚠️ The final number depends on that release's full exports-map diff; the bump PR should diff both manifests
   rather than assuming 18.
2. **The `PackageSchema` importers grew** — 4 files after cloud#2032, not the 2 the step-1 PR body first claimed
   (correction: comment `5566901682`). All are the package-format half this card re-points.
3. ⚠️ **Unverified, worth one look**: objectui `main` recently took `ab03bffae`, a gate judging spec member citations
   in published prose. Five objectui files cite cloud-subpath symbols in prose (`packages/auth/README.md:220`,
   `createAuthenticatedFetch.ts:106`, `marketplaceApi.ts:85`, `usePackageL10n.ts:6`, `PackagesPage.tsx:76`). Whether
   that gate calls them phantom once `./cloud` is gone is for the bump PR to check.
4. **Not swept**: what inside `objectstack-ai/objectstack` itself counts `@objectstack/spec` subpaths or exports-map
   entries. The sweep covered objectui only. ⛔ Stated as a gap rather than left to imply repo-wide coverage — step 3
   lands in objectstack, so this is the one that would bite it.

Claim: PM direct maintainer dispatch (no numbered round — direct-dispatch channel); step 3 of 3, all three `Blocked-by:` edges now closed

Branch: `claude/issue-16325-spec-drops-cloud-subpath`

Container & model: `L`, `mode:subagent`, `model: claude-fable-5-1` (= `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`; clause ② — deleting a published subpath export from `@objectstack/spec` is a public-surface change by definition)
Clause-②: yes
Serial constraints cleared: `#16450` closed/merged 2026-09-07T08:19Z, `objectstack-ai/objectui#8225` closed/merged 2026-09-07T17:15Z, `#16526` closed/completed 2026-09-10 — all three edges CLOSED, not merely declared discharged. No in-flight objectstack card declares `packages/spec/src/cloud/**`; the `domain:spec` seat post (#6017) has an incumbent but this dispatch runs on the direct-dispatch channel, ⛔ no seat seized.

Maintainer authorisation, verbatim (⛔ quoted, not translated): 「你直接负责派发处理」, following 「同意 A」 on #16526.

### Premise re-check at dispatch time (⛔ not inherited — the card's readings are 5 days old)

`origin/main` **`706ad0fcc`** (the card was written against `d5d8d50db`). All five work items re-verified as still undone:

| # | item | reading |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `./cloud` still exported | `packages/spec/package.json` ⇒ 1 hit |
| 2 | package-format half still under `src/cloud/` | 22 matching entries |
| 3 | `EnvironmentType` still imported by `api/discovery.zod.ts` | 1 |
| 4 | `ArtifactReferenceSchema` still imported by `api/package-api.zod.ts` | 1 |
| 5 | `packages/metadata/src/plugin.ts` still imports `@objectstack/spec/cloud` | 1 |

⚠️ The four files to delete carry **three companion test files** the card does not name: `app-store.test.ts`,
`developer-portal.test.ts`, `marketplace-admin.test.ts` (`environment-package.zod.ts` has none).

### ⭐ Three counters inside THIS repo that name `cloud` explicitly — the class that already broke step 2

Step 2 (`objectstack-ai/objectui#8360`) was FAILed in review because removing the last `@objectstack/spec/cloud`
literal broke an anti-vacuity floor pin nobody had listed. That sweep covered objectui only, and this seat said so
rather than implying it was repo-wide. It is now done for objectstack, and it found three:

1. **`packages/runtime/src/spec-subpath-alias-coverage.pin.test.ts:126`** —
   `expect(PUBLISHED_SUBPATHS).toContain('@objectstack/spec/cloud');` — an assertion that `cloud` **is** a published
   subpath, derived at `:85` from `Object.keys(specPackageJson.exports)`. It goes red the moment the entry is
   removed. `:123` is also a floor, `toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(15)` — check whether the post-deletion count still
   clears it rather than assuming.
2. **`packages/runtime/vitest.config.ts`** and **`packages/metadata/vitest.config.ts`** — alias tables enumerating
   published subpaths, `cloud` among them. Their own comments record incident #9457, where a MISSING entry made
   `@objectstack/spec/cloud` resolve to the garbage path `…/spec/src/index.ts/cloud` and die with `ENOTDIR`. A
   stale entry pointing at a deleted directory is the same failure with the sign flipped.
3. **`packages/spec/scripts/export-origins.test.ts:53`** — `['./cloud', () => import('../src/cloud/index')]`, a
   table entry that dynamically imports the cloud barrel.

### Cross-repo state, already handled — ⛔ do not re-do it

- `objectstack-ai/cloud` no longer imports any control-plane schema (step 1, merged). Its remaining
  `@objectstack/spec/cloud` importers are **4** files, all `PackageSchema` — the package-format half, whose new
  home this card decides. They are the cloud seat's to re-point **after** this lands, ⛔ not from here.
- `objectstack-ai/objectui` dropped its `export type * as Cloud` re-export (step 2, merged). Its two exports-map
  pins (`scripts/__tests__/vite-objectstack-spec-dist.test.ts:152` and `:608`, both `19`) go 19 → 18 on the objectui
  PR that bumps the spec dependency to the release carrying this deletion — that PR's job, ⛔ not this one's.
